commit 8b25816 -- Task 19 fix round (corrected the false F1-F3 detection-coverage claim; documented MLS_ALERT_EMAIL)
assertion.rationale: F17 (Task 19): infra/bicep/platform/main.bicep now adds one Microsoft.Insights/actionGroups (email receiver, the same sponsor address scripts/bootstrap/03-budget.ps1 already notifies) and two Microsoft.Insights/scheduledQueryRules against the Log Analytics workspace F9 routes diagnostics to -- a Key Vault AuditEvent denied-result spike (httpStatusCode_d >= 300 in the AzureDiagnostics table, the destination F9's diagnostic settings use by default) and an Azure SQL failed-login spike (SQLSecurityAuditEvents, succeeded_s == "false"). Both are named verbatim by F17's own Fix text ("Key Vault access-denied spikes, SQL failed-login spikes") and that is this rationale's justification -- NOT detection coverage of F1, F2 or F3. F1/F2/F3 are app-layer authentication bypasses: an unauthenticated caller reaches the app, and the app's own already-privileged managed identity then talks to Key Vault and SQL successfully, with no access-denied event and no failed login anywhere in that path -- the platform sees a legitimate identity doing legitimate things, so neither rule would ever fire for that exploit class. What these two rules actually detect is narrower and different in kind: probing or misconfiguration against Key Vault and Azure SQL directly (an unexpected denial, an unexpected failed login), generalising F9's collection to the two surfaces that hold the estate's real credentials (Key Vault: the Direct Line secret, mcp-auth-token) and its Entra-only workload auth (F13's grants). A third rule for Container Apps restart counts (the brief's own suggestion) was deliberately dropped: the individual container app resources a meaningful restart metric would attach to do not exist at L6 -- they deploy at L7 -- so a metricAlert cannot be authored here without an app resource id this template never sees, and no log-based proxy at the environment scope has a Microsoft-documented contract precise enough to write with confidence absent a live workspace. A cost/usage-spike rule was also deliberately not duplicated: Task 17/F15 already added Forecasted budget notifications for that gap. Both rules evaluate every 15 minutes; Azure's scheduled-query-rule cost boundary sits at 5 minutes (flat-priced at or above it, materially more only below it), so 15 minutes sits inside that flat band rather than at some specially cheap point within it, keeping combined cost on the order of a dollar or two per month against the $200/30-day credit. SI-4 is tailored out of NIST SP 800-171 but system monitoring for indicators of compromise is exactly what CMMC assessors probe; F17 was this control's sole contributor, and with F17 closed this control closes outright. Checked: no other finding in compliance/findings/2026-08-26-prepublication-review.md cites SI-4.

recommendation: None outstanding for this control. A regression here -- the action group or either scheduledQueryRule removed from platform/main.bicep without replacement, or both rules' queries stop matching the AzureDiagnostics schema F9's diagnostic settings actually populate -- would reopen it.
